title.en: Density height, interval area and standardization invariance

summary: Separate density height from interval probability and confirm invariance under standardization and decorative geometry.
objective: Reported probabilities stay in the unit interval, a zero-width interval reports zero, and decorative depth changes no number.
applies_when: A scene shades an interval under a continuous density and reports a probability.
The density belongs to a location-scale family such as the normal, so standardized bounds are meaningful.
The density is drawn as an extruded or otherwise decorated solid.
intent_signals: the density value is above one, is that wrong
example_prompts: Check the interval probability readout under this normal curve.

principles: Density is not probability: the height of a continuous density may exceed one, while probability is an area over an interval and lies between zero and one.
A zero-width interval has zero probability even where the density is positive, which is the case that exposes a display multiplying height by a fixed width.

Standardizing removes the parameters within a location-scale family, so at fixed standardized bounds the interval probability does not depend on the location or scale; outside such a family the invariance does not hold and the check does not apply.
implementation: Reject a non-finite location or a nonfinite or nonpositive scale before evaluating anything, declare how reversed bounds are handled, and compute interval probability from a difference of cumulative values rather than by summing rendered bar heights, recording which cumulative implementation is used.

Evaluate the degenerate interval with coincident endpoints, a reversed interval, and an interval far out in the tail where subtracting two cumulative values close to one cancels; compare that case against a tail-stable reference such as a complementary cumulative form, or declare the supported range and the absolute accuracy outside it.
Hold standardized bounds fixed while varying the mean and standard deviation across several values and record the probability each time.
If the density is extruded into a solid, state in the artifact that the extrusion carries no probability and confirm that the reported number does not scale with it.
observable_checks: Reported probability stays within zero and one for every supported input, and a zero-width interval reports exactly zero while the density readout stays positive inside the declared display range; far into the tail the density can underflow to zero, which is reported as underflow rather than as a probability statement.

Within the location-scale family, fixed standardized bounds give an unchanged probability as location and scale vary, within the accuracy of the cumulative implementation, which is reported alongside the value; nonfinite location or nonfinite or nonpositive scale is rejected rather than plotted.
Changing extrusion depth or any decorative scale changes no reported probability; if it does, geometry is being used as arithmetic.

known_limits: Checks the density and area relationship in the declared model; selecting an interval implies no inferential statement.
Authored verification guidance; no computation or render was run for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: A normal variable with mean mu and standard deviation sigma is standardized by subtracting the mean and dividing by the standard deviation, which gives a standard normal variable with mean zero and standard deviation one.
claims.scope: The declared normal model; probability statements refer to intervals rather than to individual points.
